findings.claim: L78 records the owner's reply as the verbatim word "aprieno" and reads it as "apruebo" by interpretation. The approval of a byte-for-byte artifact therefore rests on a typo read, which is a weak audit trail. L77 handled the same kind of typo ("si me fyst") with the same "read:" convention, so this is consistent, but a reader cannot tell whether the approval covers the Learning section the parent added in the same turn.

The closing line says T27's L60-based description is superseded, but the diff does not edit T27 or L60 themselves. Readers of T27 further up the file get the stale Gentleman-based description unless they reach L78. The same applies to T26 and the Codex persona part of T31/T22, which L77 still describes as waiting. The cross-reference lives only in the Log.

evidence: The diff only appends L78 to the Log of odd/tasks/labdrian-orchestrator-opencode.md; no code or config changes.

The embedded style text matches the L77 summary: Principle, Replies, Rigor and Language are all present, plus the new Learning section, which L78 attributes to the owner's "no me gusta repetir errores".
The rule text quoted for owner-rules matches the L77 wording verbatim.
L78 uses a four-backtick fence around a block that itself contains only a three-dash front matter, so the nesting is valid.
